title: How Corporations Can Mitigate an AI Jobocalypse
gist: Raghuram Rajan argues AI-driven job displacement is coming but its pace is highly uncertain and depends on firm-level adoption speed, citing a US Census survey showing only 20% of small firms versus 37% of large firms currently use AI in any business function, with corporations needing to be enlisted alongside government policy to cushion the effects.

themes.theme: Pace and scale of AI-driven job displacement

insights.claim: AI-related job displacement is coming, but no one knows how fast it will proceed, how far it will go, or which sectors it will affect most, with much depending on how quickly individual firms apply the technology to their operations.
insights.speaker: RAGHURAM G. RAJAN
insights.so_what: Investors should treat AI labor-displacement timelines as highly uncertain and firm-adoption-dependent rather than assuming a uniform, imminent shock across sectors.
insights.quote: AI-related job displacement is coming, though no one knows how fast it will proceed, how far it will go, and which sectors it will affect most.

insights.claim: A recent US Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey found that only 20% of firms with fewer than 20 employees currently use AI in any business function, compared to 37% of businesses with at least 250 employees.
insights.speaker: RAGHURAM G. RAJAN
insights.so_what: Current AI adoption rates remain low even among large employers, suggesting corporate AI-driven productivity and labor effects are still early-stage rather than fully priced in.
insights.quote: A recent US Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey indicates that only 20% of firms with fewer than 20 employees currently use AI, compared to 37% of businesses with at least 250 employees.
insights.locator: A recent US Census Bureau Business Trends

insights.claim: Even the 37% AI-usage figure among large firms is described as quite meager given the survey's low threshold for a firm to count as using AI, which was simply whether AI is used 'in any business function.'
insights.speaker: RAGHURAM G. RAJAN
insights.so_what: Pushes back on narratives of rapid, widespread corporate AI adoption; investors should be skeptical of claims that AI displacement is already broad-based.
insights.quote: While larger firms are doing more with the technology, 37% is still quite meager considering the survey’s low threshold for answering in the affirmative (whether AI is used “in any business function”).
insights.locator: While larger firms are doing more

insights.claim: Corporations will need to be enlisted in minimizing the effects of AI-related job displacement in the name of social solidarity, with governments considering policy incentives and large employers considering their own long-term interests.
insights.speaker: RAGHURAM G. RAJAN
insights.so_what: Signals a likely policy direction of government incentives aimed at large employers to manage AI transition costs, worth monitoring for regulatory or tax-incentive developments affecting large-cap employers.
insights.quote: corporations will need to be enlisted in minimizing its effects in the name of social solidarity
insights.locator: Even if AI-related job displacement is less severe
